This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at

## Evidence — verified finding

```
`Expr::InterpolatedText(Vec<Expr>)` is declared at src/parser.rs:56 and is handled by four consumers — src/analyzer.rs:437, src/interpreter.rs:1515, src/formatter.rs:734 and src/linter.rs:381 — but the parser has ZERO construction sites: `grep -n 'InterpolatedText' src/parser.rs` prints exactly one line, the declaration at :56. The text-literal arm at src/parser.rs:2023-2026 does `TokenKind::Text(s) => { self.advance(); Ok(Expr::Text(s.clone())) }`, passing the braces through verbatim, so all four consumers are dead code. Verified against the built binary: `set name to "Bob"` then `say "Hello, {name}!"` prints `Hello, {name}!` and exits 0 — the NAME, not the value. SPEC.md:293-298 (`### String Interpolation`, `set greeting to "Hello, {name}!"`, `set message to "Value: {x + y}"`) and SPEC.md:526 document the form as working; AGENTS.md section 2 lists "Trailing-comma and `{interp}` string syntax" as a LANGUAGE INVARIANT that must not silently change, so the invariant is violated today, not merely missing. `rb run examples/hello.rb` prints `Hello, {name}!` as its third line, and the example sweep in rbops/verify.sh runs it and only checks the exit code. A GREEN test pins the broken behaviour as correct: tests/test_text.rb:37 `test "text: braces are ordinary characters in a text literal"` asserts `expect "Hello, {name}!" to be "Hello, {name}!"` at :41 and `expect length("Hello, {name}!") to be 14` at :42, with a comment at :38 admitting the VM does not substitute. This defect was found and recorded as severity blocker by THREE separate phases — phases/phase-003/FINDINGS.md:44-64, phases/phase-008/FINDINGS.md:11-34 and phases/phase-016/FINDINGS.md:77 — and no phase was ever written for it, because FINDINGS.md is a report and the manifest is the queue.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer

## Goal

Make `say "Hello, {name}!"` print the bound value, on both VMs, by constructing the `Expr::InterpolatedText` the AST already declares and four subsystems already handle.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-047
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `set name to "World"` followed by `say "Hello, {name}!"` prints `Hello, World!` and exits 0, verified BOTH with `rb run` and with `rb vm` on the output of `rb compile`; the full output of both commands is pasted into REPORT.md
- [ ] `set x to 2` / `set y to 3` / `say "Value: {x + y}"` prints `Value: 5` — an arbitrary EXPRESSION inside braces is evaluated, not just a bare name, matching SPEC.md:297
- [ ] `grep -n 'InterpolatedText' src/parser.rs` returns MORE THAN ONE line and the construction site is pasted into REPORT.md; it is no longer a declared-but-unbuilt variant
- [ ] a text literal with NO braces is unchanged: `say "plain"` prints `plain`, and a literal holding a lone `{`, a lone `}`, or `"{"` round-trips exactly — a brace pair is markup ONLY when it is well formed
- [ ] tests/test_text.rb:37 is CORRECTED, not deleted: `text: braces are ordinary characters in a text literal` is rewritten to assert real substitution (`expect "Hello, {name}!" to be "Hello, Alice!"`), the `length(...) to be 14` assertion at :42 is replaced by the length of the SUBSTITUTED text, and a test asserts that named test still exists and still passes
- [ ] edge tests named edge_* cover: a brace pair around an unknown name (a clean AnalyzerError naming it, NOT a literal `{name}` printed), nested braces, an empty brace pair `"{}"`, an unbalanced closing brace, a brace pair inside a nested record or list, and interpolation of a list, a record and an object
- [ ] edge tests assert a FAILURE for an interpolation whose expression raises — the failure names the string's line and column, and `try`/`catch` around the statement catches it on BOTH engines
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0; `rb run examples/hello.rb` now prints `Hello, World!` on its third line, and that output is pasted into REPORT.md
- [ ] the four existing consumers (src/analyzer.rs:437, src/interpreter.rs:1515, src/formatter.rs:734, src/linter.rs:381) now actually run: a lint warning and a formatter pass over an interpolated string are pinned by tests, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(dead_code)` added
